patch.value:
GitHub report: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1266

The SDK budget compactor selects the largest fitting prefix of the chosen reducible collection by measuring the complete rendered JSON/TOON envelope at each candidate. Measurements include rebased producer or universal cursors, count/applied_limit fields, truncation disclosure, and session charges. Hidden row declarations remain available for nested arrays/maps without consuming emitted tokens. Top-level session facts are charged before prefix selection as well as during final accounting.

A complete response and a partial response have different required metadata. The maximal-prefix and monotonic-request guarantees apply within the truncated-envelope regime; crossing from a complete response into a partial response can require more metadata. Reserving unused continuation metadata on every complete response would conflict with no-op receipt elision. This boundary is documented rather than hidden by a blanket monotonicity claim.

Regression evidence covers increasing list limits, one-more-row infeasibility, nested object maps, mixed activity/session facts, cursor offsets, and real temporary-workspace Node/Bun acceptance. The generated token measurement records 77 contract summaries rather than 68 within the unchanged 4500-token ceiling. See comments and linked test runs for current verification status.

Choose the largest prefix fitting the complete rendered partial-response envelope; increasing requests within the truncated-envelope regime must not exhibit halving oscillation. Keep applied limits, cursor offsets, nested row declarations, and session charges consistent. Document the unavoidable metadata-cost difference at the complete-to-partial boundary.
